correctness.rationale: For odd characteristic \(p\), neither \(d=2p^e+1\) nor \(m=d-2\) is divisible by \(p\). The coordinatewise-square morphism of the smooth Fermat curve is finite generically étale and geometrically injective, hence birational; pullback degree \(2d\) identifies its image with the irreducible degree-\(2d\) Heron-type equation G. The Gauss map is this morphism followed by \(q\)-Frobenius. Differentiation of G proves precisely \(3d\) coordinate-axis singular points, each étale-locally \(v^2-4u^d\)=0, hence unibranch with delta (d-1)/2; the genus formula checks. Differentiating G at square images yields the exponent-m bidual map, which is generically birational by gcd(m,d)=1, giving degree md. Field arithmetic scripts tested the F9 and F25 cases without being used for infinite conclusions.

broader_coverage.reasoning: For odd \(p\) and prime power \(q=p^r\), an equality \(q^2+q+1=2p^e+1\) requires \(q(q+1)=2p^e\), hence \(q+1=2p^{e-r}\). Since \(q+1\) is prime to \(p\), one must have \(e=r\) and \(q=1\), impossible. The specialized Fermat dual theorem of Komeda therefore does not cover this family. No inspected broad source gives the complete result as an automatic stated corollary.
